measurements.name: nhs-ae-four-hour-decline

source.publisher: NHS England, A&E Attendances and Emergency Admissions statistical work area
source.requests_note: 102 monthly provider-level CSV GETs plus 11 year-page GETs (~80 KB each) to enumerate the URLs; measured 1.2 s wall clock on the coordinator (1.9 GiB class host)
source.worker_provenance: the publisher's CDN serves HTTP 202 with an empty body to datacenter IPs (measured 2026-10-21, job nhsae-001), so job nhsae-002 consumed the same bytes from staging release source-nhsae-001 (asset 661561799, sha256 verified on arrival and per-file by build.py)

label.within4h_rate: 1 - Attendances over 4hrs Type 1 / A&E attendances Type 1
label.note: fixed thresholds measured near-uniform rates and were refused (record: <95% -> holdout 99.9% positive; <80% -> 95.8%); the m/m direction label is threshold-free

volume_gate.applies_to: both the feature month M and the target month M+1

panel.note: each month is published in exactly one file, so the prefer-latest-upload revision policy never had anything to dedup on the 2026-10-21 vintage (it is still implemented and reported)

measurements.clustered_events_note: distinct_events counts distinct positive Org Codes per window - positives cluster within providers, so this is the conservative independent-unit count
measurements.schema_evolution: 16 data columns 2018-04..2020-07 (with 'Number of' prefixes in 2018-19); booked-appointment columns from 2020-08 (22 columns); unnamed padding columns from 2024-09 (28 header fields); booked columns parsed but not shipped - they are absent for train feature months 2018-12..2020-07, so shipping them would be a split-dependent prediction-timing defect

reference_baselines.note: stdlib rank AUC measured at construction on the written rows; every score is a prediction-time-safe single feature

runner_contract_baseline.note: measured on the released bytes fetched from staging (digest-verified, gate re-accepted before scoring), below the mean-reversion reference (0.5659 eval / 0.6562 holdout) which is the bar a competent model must beat

source.name: NHS England - A&E Attendances and Emergency Admissions, statistical work area (monthly provider-level CSVs)

rules: Code and documentation: MIT by default.
Our rights in a derived compilation: CC0-1.0 by default.
The source's own terms are preserved and never relicensed; the compilation dedication covers only our contribution.

Each dataset must use terms compatible with its sources. CC0 is NOT a blanket override of upstream terms: attribution, share-alike and non-commercial requirements from a source are carried through unchanged.
A source whose licence terms cannot be read is not published at all.
The chosen terms are declared per dataset in candidates/<id>/license.json and recorded in the release manifest, so the manifest cannot drift from the decision.
